sources.entry: Espial - Web-based bookmarking server that supports multiple user accounts. AGPL-3.0 Haskell

summary.one_liner: Espial is an open-source, self-hosted, web-based bookmarking server with multiple user accounts and SQLite storage.
summary.what_it_does: Espial stores bookmarks in a SQLite database and supports multiple user accounts, primarily for self-hosted use. Users can add bookmarks through a browser bookmarklet that pre-fills URL, title, and selected text, or via a JSON API (/api/add and /api/addBulk) authenticated with an API key. Bookmarks can be imported from Pinboard-style JSON, Firefox, and Netscape HTML files, and exported in JSON, Netscape HTML, or notes JSON formats through the CLI or web UI. Bookmarks can be marked private or shared, flagged "to read", and given tags and slugs. The web UI is available in 15 languages selectable per account, and optional archive backends (Internet Archive Wayback Machine or a local ArchiveBox 0.7 instance) can save page snapshots.
use_cases: share bookmarks with other users on a server
save links from the browser with a bookmarklet
archive bookmarked pages to Wayback Machine or ArchiveBox
how_to_run: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 docker run --name espial -p 9090:3000 -v espial-data:/app/data -d jonschoning/espial:espial
docker exec espial ./migration createuser --userName myusername --userPassword myuserpassword
stack exec migration -- createuser --userName myusername --userPassword myuserpassword
notable: Bookmarklet for one-click saving of the current page with title and selected text
JSON API with API keys, single and bulk add endpoints
In-process TLS with certificate reload every 12 hours or on SIGHUP
Optional archiving to Internet Archive Wayback Machine or local ArchiveBox
Subpath hosting support via APPROOT and reverse proxy prefix stripping
caveats: ArchiveBox backend stores all archive data in one global index, so it suits single-user instances best
Reverse proxy is recommended for production; in-process TLS is described as suited to simple local or LAN setups
Setup from source requires Haskell tooling (Stack or GHCup)
keywords: save web pages to read later
